clue.text: Stylish young woman living in Cyprus

indicators.note: the young woman is said to reside within the island's abbreviation, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: CY is the international vehicle code for Cyprus
a lass is a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: A fashionable girl who has made her home on a Mediterranean island.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone or something with class is elegant and fashionable, a close synonym of the clue's adjective.

clue.text: Disaster! Alma got lost in large town

indicators.note: the jumbled name is placed within the word for a big town

parts.note: a city is a large town

indicators.note: a name that has got lost is muddled up, signalling its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone panics because Alma has gone missing somewhere in a big town.
explanation.definitionFit: A calamity is a catastrophe or great misfortune, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Could be gun trouble involving evil American native

parts.note: a gun is a firearm, an arm

indicators.note: the word for fuss wraps around the word for wickedness, so one encloses the other

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble
ill can mean evil, as in 'ill will'

explanation.surface: A firearm causing problems is linked to some wicked plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Could be' just hints that a gun is one kind of arm. The animal is native to the Americas.
explanation.definitionFit: This armoured mammal is native to the Americas, so the definition is a description of its origin.

clue.text: Special tax on Spain's new bread

parts.note: a toll is a charge or levy, a kind of tax
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A one-off levy imposed on a newly baked Spanish loaf.
explanation.definitionFit: Stollen is a German fruit loaf eaten at Christmas, so it is an example of bread.

clue.text: State copper left university to begin studying branch of Maths

parts.note: Cal. is an abbreviation for California, a US state
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: to begin points to just the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A police officer from a state has quit college to start learning mathematics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State copper' reads as a state police officer, but it is two separate pieces: CAL and CU.
explanation.definitionFit: Calculus, the study of rates of change and integration, is one of the major fields of mathematics.

clue.text: In old, old Gallic area rebuilding church could be described thus

definitions.text: In old, old Gallic area rebuilding church could be described thus

indicators.note: rebuilding means putting the letters back together in a new arrangement

parts.note: O again stands for old
O again stands for old

explanation.surface: Restoring a church in an ancient region of France would interest a scholar of the past.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: work on an ancient church in an old part of Gaul is the business of digs and ruins.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes anything to do with studying ancient remains, which an old Gallic church restoration would be.

clue.text: Person one can call on to learn diplomacy

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn by heart
tact is sensitivity or diplomacy in dealing with people

explanation.surface: Someone you can visit to pick up lessons in delicate negotiation.
explanation.walkthrough: CON meaning 'to study' is an old, mainly literary sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A contact is someone in your network whom you can approach for help or information.

clue.text: Unfasten John's empty suitcase

parts.note: john is slang for a toilet, as is loo

indicators.note: an empty word has its insides removed, leaving only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A man called John has an unpacked case for his travels.
explanation.walkthrough: John is not a man here: 'john' is American slang for a toilet, as 'loo' is British.
explanation.definitionFit: To loose something is to release or untie it, a slightly old-fashioned verb sense.

clue.text: Thwarted lust starts to render youth hot with anger

indicators.note: thwarted desire is upset and twisted, so these letters are rearranged
starts to means the opening letters of the next words are taken

explanation.surface: Frustrated desire makes a young man furious and heated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thwarted' turns LUST into SULT; RY are the starts of 'render' and 'youth'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sultry describes heat, both of oppressive weather and of a passionate or inflamed temper.

clue.text: Excessive use of strikes is settled in stormy Irish debates?

indicators.note: the little word is lodged within the other letters, so it is placed inside them
stormy debates are turbulent, signalling that the letters are churned up

explanation.surface: Industrial unrest is argued over in heated sessions of an Irish assembly.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a playful definition: the phrase was a 1960s-70s label, used abroad, for Britain's frequent strikes.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a mid-twentieth-century nickname for the UK's frequent industrial action and strikes.

clue.text: Bobbysoxer's first to get into car to get to dance

indicators.note: the letter is said to climb inside the vehicle, so it is put within it

parts.note: a limo, short for limousine, is a luxury car

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the bobbysoxer

explanation.surface: A teenage girl climbs into a car first to go dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: A bobbysoxer was an American teenage girl of the 1940s.
explanation.definitionFit: The limbo is a Caribbean dance in which performers lean backwards under a lowered bar.

clue.text: Diamond's new part broadcast in this music

parts.note: rock is slang for a diamond

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard by listeners, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a role is a part in a play or film

explanation.surface: A singer called Diamond has a fresh role on air in this kind of music.
explanation.walkthrough: Neil Diamond tempts as the singer, but 'Diamond' simply gives ROCK.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition points to a style of popular music, the 1950s genre built on rhythm and blues.

clue.text: Daft lump almost floundered in part of estuary

indicators.note: something that floundered struggled clumsily, signalling a rearrangement of letters
almost means the word falls short by its final letter

explanation.surface: A clumsy oaf staggered about in the muddy shallows of a river mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims LUMP to LUM; 'floundered' then rearranges DAFT LUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A mudflat is a stretch of muddy land exposed at low tide, typically found in an estuary.

clue.text: Australian team beaten by retired sport enthusiast

indicators.note: beaten letters are knocked about, so they are rearranged
retired means withdrawn backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: RU is Rugby Union, a sport

explanation.surface: An Aussie side lost to a former athlete who was keen on the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beaten' turns TEAM into MATE; 'retired' reverses RU to UR.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur is someone who pursues a pastime for love of it, so a devotee or fan.

clue.text: Quirky personal test included time and time again for such researchers

indicators.note: the two small letters are taken into the mixture, so they go inside it
something quirky is odd and twisted, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a second T for time

explanation.surface: An odd personal test is used repeatedly by those searching for gifted people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time and time again' looks like 'repeatedly' but supplies two separate letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Scouts who look for gifted performers, who might use a personal test to find them, are such researchers.

clue.text: Yorkshire town's favourite treatment for important people

parts.note: Redcar is a seaside town in North Yorkshire, England
a pet is a favourite, as in 'teacher's pet'

explanation.surface: A northern English town's preferred way of welcoming dignitaries.
explanation.walkthrough: REDCAR is a seaside town on the North Yorkshire coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Rolling out a crimson carpet is the ceremonial welcome given to VIPs and celebrities.

clue.text: Initially moderate opinions for fear that journalist is annoyed

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the following words

parts.note: lest means for fear that
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: Mild views, worried a reporter would be upset by them.
explanation.definitionFit: To molest in its older sense is to pester, bother or harass, which matches being annoyed.

clue.text: Crow parrot played for time

indicators.note: for signals that one piece stands in place of another

parts.note: a cockatoo is a crested parrot
doodled means played idly, as on a musical instrument

explanation.surface: A talking bird copied a black bird to pass the time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crow' looks like the bird, but it is the verb: a cockerel's call. DOODLED replaces the T in COCKATOO.
explanation.definitionFit: The cry of a rooster at dawn is called a crow, and this is its traditional English rendering.

clue.text: Outfit restricts funds

parts.note: kit is a set of clothes or equipment, an outfit
ties means restricts or binds

explanation.surface: A company limits the money it spends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outfit' suggests a firm, but it gives KIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitty is a pool of money collected for shared use, so the plural means pots of money.

clue.text: Al pried craftily and understood mouthed comments

indicators.note: craftily suggests cunning rearrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: Al snooped cunningly and grasped what people were silently saying.
explanation.definitionFit: To lipread is to follow speech by watching lip movements; its past tense is spelt the same.

clue.text: Short notice? Book quickly, say

indicators.note: short means the word is cut by its last letter

parts.note: an advert is a public notice

explanation.surface: With little warning, you'd better reserve right away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks 'quickly' as an example of the part of speech.
explanation.definitionFit: The word 'quickly' modifies a verb, so it is an instance of this grammatical class.

clue.text: Editor backs revised set-up and passes authority to someone else

indicators.note: backs means the abbreviation runs backwards
revised means the letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: An editor supports a reorganisation and hands over control to a colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backs' looks like support, but it reverses ED to DE; 'revised' rearranges SETUP.
explanation.definitionFit: To depute is to delegate, appointing another to act with one's power.

clue.text: Nut's cold afternoon lying in enclosure

indicators.note: the two letters rest within the enclosure, so they are placed inside it

parts.note: a pen is an enclosure for animals
A can stand for afternoon, as in p.m. abbreviations

explanation.surface: A crazy person spends a chilly afternoon lying about in a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an edible nut from a hickory tree native to North America.

clue.text: Wearing a touch of pink material is suitable

parts.note: in means wearing, as in 'in a hat'

indicators.note: a touch of means just a small part, the first letter

parts.note: lace is a delicate fabric

explanation.surface: Putting on a hint of pink fabric is fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in place is appropriate or fitting, as in 'that remark was not in place'.

clue.text: Chana delicacy only half cooked in spicy dish

indicators.note: cooked suggests ingredients mixed up, so the letters are rearranged
half means the first half of the word, its first four letters

explanation.surface: A chickpea treat that has been only partly cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: Chana is a South Asian chickpea dish; half of DELICACY is DELI, and 'cooked' mixes CHANA DELI.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a Mexican tortilla rolled round a filling and served in a chilli sauce.

clue.text: Former president receives a threat finally living in exile

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: finally points to the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: An ex-president, now threatened, lives abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: An expatriate lives outside their native country, sometimes by choice and sometimes banished.

clue.text: Black bird woman had driven away

parts.note: B is an abbreviation for black, as on pencils
the ani is a tropical American cuckoo
she'd is short for she had

explanation.surface: A dark bird driven off by a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To be banished is to be expelled or sent into exile, so forced to leave.

clue.text: Improved diet altered principals of existence daily

indicators.note: altered means changed in order, so the letters are rearranged
principals of plays on principal meaning first, so the first letters are taken

explanation.surface: A changed eating plan has bettered the basics of everyday life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'principals' (chiefs) puns on 'principles', taking the initial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Text that has been revised and corrected has been refined, which is the sense of the definition.
